ai.definition: Computing on device refers to the capability of running artificial intelligence (AI) models locally on a device rather than sending data to a remote server for processing.
ai.howItWorks: This technology allows AI models to run directly on the hardware of a device, such as smartphones or IoT devices, by optimizing the model's architecture and using specialized hardware accelerators. This minimizes latency and power consumption compared to cloud-based solutions where data must be transmitted over networks.
ai.problemSolved: It addresses the challenges of high latency in real-time applications and excessive power consumption when transmitting large amounts of data to remote servers for processing.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves optimizing existing hardware or designing new specialized hardware accelerators that can efficiently run AI models. This includes integrating these accelerators into devices like smartphones, tablets, and IoT gadgets.
ai.buildProcess: Building computing on device solutions requires expertise in both software and hardware engineering. It involves model optimization techniques such as quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation to reduce the computational requirements of AI models. Hardware design focuses on creating efficient silicon that can handle these optimized models without significant power draw.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the complexity of optimizing AI models for different devices, the cost of developing specialized hardware accelerators, and the need for robust software frameworks to support these optimizations across various platforms.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as more applications require low-latency and privacy-preserving solutions. However, challenges remain in standardizing hardware and software interfaces.
ai.regulation: Regulatory considerations include data privacy laws that may impact how devices handle local AI processing of sensitive information. There are also potential issues with the security of locally processed data.
ai.risks: Technical risks include ensuring model accuracy when optimized for low-power devices, managing thermal constraints in small form factors, and maintaining compatibility across different hardware platforms. Market risks involve competition from cloud providers and the need to balance power efficiency with computational capabilities.
ai.profitability: Profitability is variable depending on the specific market segment and business model. Companies that can offer efficient, secure, and privacy-preserving solutions may find success in this space.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving energy efficiency, expanding model complexity support, and enhancing integration with existing cloud infrastructure for hybrid solutions.

glossary.def: The delay between when an input is given to a system and the corresponding output is produced.
A process that reduces the precision of weights in neural networks, making them smaller and faster to compute without significantly compromising accuracy.

subsystems.name: Compressed model
subsystems.role: the neural network itself, shrunk to fit a phone's memory and power budget.

subsystems.name: Compute accelerator
subsystems.role: runs the matrix maths without draining the battery.

subsystems.name: Memory system
subsystems.role: feeds a compute engine that is starved of bandwidth long before it runs out of arithmetic.

subsystems.name: Runtime and compiler
subsystems.role: turns a trained model into a schedule of operations the chip can execute.

subsystems.name: Storage and update layer
subsystems.role: stores model files and replaces them without breaking the device.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal manager
subsystems.role: keeps sustained performance from collapsing into throttling.

buildSteps.title: Train the model
buildSteps.detail: Large datasets and many accelerators produce an accurate but oversized network in a data centre.

buildSteps.title: Compress it
buildSteps.detail: Pruning removes near-useless connections, distillation trains a smaller student network, and quantization maps floating-point weights onto 8-bit or 4-bit integers.

buildSteps.title: Compile for the target chip
buildSteps.detail: The runtime fuses operations, chooses kernels written for that NPU or GPU, and plans how tensors move between memory tiers.

buildSteps.title: Bind it into the application
buildSteps.detail: The model file ships inside an app or operating system, called through a framework API rather than a network request.

buildSteps.title: Validate on real hardware
buildSteps.detail: Accuracy, latency, memory footprint and battery drain are measured on the actual devices and chips being targeted.

buildSteps.title: Ship and version
buildSteps.detail: The model is delivered in an app update or operating system release, with fallbacks for older hardware.

buildSteps.title: Run in production
buildSteps.detail: Inference happens locally; telemetry (where privacy permits) reports crashes and latency rather than sending user data away.

buildSteps.title: Improve from the field
buildSteps.detail: Curated samples or on-device learning loops feed a retrained model back into the next release.

prerequisites.why: general-purpose CPUs cannot run modern neural networks at acceptable speed per watt.
without 4–8 bit integer weights, most models simply do not fit in device memory.
compact transformer and convolutional designs set the ceiling on what a device can run.
each accelerator vendor still needs its own kernels and toolchain, so models are not portable for free.
personalisation without sending raw data to a server is demonstrated but not routine.

pathway.milestone: speech recognition, translation, photo processing and small vision models running locally on phones and laptops
billion-parameter language models running on flagship phones and PCs
pathway.unlocks: assistants that keep working with no connectivity.

pathway.milestone: on-device personalisation and federated training at scale
pathway.unlocks: models that adapt to one user without their data leaving the device.

pathway.milestone: always-on local agents coordinating several models across a device's chips
pathway.unlocks: a shift of routine inference from data centres to the edge, cutting latency and energy.
